title: Build Cache Cleanup
description: Delete regeneratable *.o object files from a build cache while keeping sources and the output binary.
scenario: The CI runner's cache directory /var/tmp/buildcache has grown fat with object files (*.o) that the compiler regenerates anyway. Free the space: remove every *.o file in the tree, keep the src/ sources and the output/ binary untouched, and record how many object files you removed in /home/intern/cleanup-report.txt as object-files-removed=4.
symptoms: /var/tmp/buildcache is much larger than its git history suggests
Four *.o object files sit in the cache tree
src/ (sources) and output/ (the built binary) must survive untouched
The cleanup count must be reported in /home/intern/cleanup-report.txt
mission: Delete all 4 *.o files under /var/tmp/buildcache, keep src/ and output/ intact, and write `object-files-removed=4` into /home/intern/cleanup-report.txt.

hints.title: Preview before delete
hints.content: Run `find … -name '*.o'` without -delete first and eyeball the list — deleting is forever.

hints.title: The -delete action
hints.content: `find dir -name '*.o' -delete` removes every match in the whole tree, in one command. No wildcards in a rm that could mis-expand.

hints.title: Quote the glob
hints.content: If you use rm instead, quote it: `sudo find … -exec rm {} +` or `rm '*.o'` — an unquoted *.o only matches the CURRENT directory's files.

hints.title: Report the count
hints.content: The number of matches from the preview IS the number removed — here, 4.

acceptance_criteria.description: no *.o files remain anywhere under the build cache
